one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban profiles the newly appointed CJ Maria Lourdes P. A. Sereno, starting with her embodiment of Aquino's 'kung walang corrupt, walang mahirap' through her unique law-and-economics formation: valedictorian at UP Law, economics degree from Ateneo, LLM from Michigan, academic work in civil/commercial/trade law, AIM Policy Center executive directorship, 25-year private practice, and (with ret. Justice Florentino Feliciano) winning the NAIA Terminal 3 arbitration against the Philippine government in Washington and Singapore. He recounts the origin moment of her first SC appointment: at the GMA7 60th anniversary at the Makati Shangri-la on July 30, 2010, the author introduced her to P-Noy as a 'super lawyer-economist' who could link the President's program to the judiciary; Sereno immediately told P-Noy she had briefed him on the Japan-Philippines EPA when he was still a senator and that he had followed her advice; P-Noy lit up and winked at the author -- days later the Palace announced her appointment. As CJ, Sereno holds multiple records: youngest associate justice at 50 under the 1987 Constitution; most junior associate justice (ranked 12th) to become CJ; and projected to serve 18 years as CJ (second only to Arellano's 19 years, 1901-1920, but exceeding him in total SC service). She is simultaneously insider (2 years as associate justice: knows the internal dynamics) and outsider (fresh enough to reform). Her vision statement, quoted in full, commits to: regaining the public trust needed for Congress to entrust the judiciary with funds; disclosing case disposal rates, COA audits, and all fund statuses; seeking the best and brightest to be a generation of upright judges; and being 'the first to be daily tested' against the highest integrity standards.
